pairs.source_text: Quintus Marcius Luci filius, Spurius Postumius Luci filius consules senatum consoluerunt nonis Octobribus, apud aedem Duelonai.
pairs.question: Quibus consulibus senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus factum est?
pairs.answer: Q. Marcio et Sp. Postumio consulibus.
pairs.question_en: Under which consuls was the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus passed?
pairs.answer_en: In the consulship of Quintus Marcius and Spurius Postumius (186 BC).
pairs.derivation: Dating fact of the prescript: the decree was passed under the consuls Q. Marcius (Philippus) and Sp. Postumius (Albinus), i.e. 186 BC — the same consuls under whom Livy 39.8-19 narrates the Bacchanalian affair. Anchored to the named decree; single verifiable answer supported verbatim (archaic consoluerunt = consuluerunt). The consular date of the most famous surviving senatus consultum is ambient knowledge for the well-read.

pairs.source_text: Quintus Marcius Luci filius, Spurius Postumius Luci filius consules senatum consoluerunt nonis Octobribus, apud aedem Duelonai.
pairs.question: Apud cuius deae aedem consules senatum de Bacchanalibus consuluerunt?
pairs.question_en: At the temple of which goddess did the consuls consult the senate about the Bacchanalia?
pairs.answer_en: At the temple of Bellona.
pairs.derivation: Place fact of the prescript: the senate met apud aedem Duelonai — Duelona being the archaic form of Bellona. Anchored to the decree and its subject; single named-goddess answer supported verbatim (the answer normalizes the archaic spelling of the same name). That this celebrated decree was passed at the temple of Bellona is standard textbook knowledge of the document.

pairs.source_text: Quintus Marcius Luci filius, Spurius Postumius Luci filius consules senatum consoluerunt nonis Octobribus, apud aedem Duelonai.
pairs.question: Quo die Q. Marcius et Sp. Postumius consules senatum de Bacchanalibus consuluerunt?
pairs.question_en: On what day did the consuls Q. Marcius and Sp. Postumius consult the senate about the Bacchanalia?
pairs.answer_en: On the Nones of October (7 October).
pairs.derivation: Calendar fact of the prescript: the senate was consulted nonis Octobribus (7 October 186 BC). Anchored by the decree and the named consuls; single date answer supported verbatim. The prescript of this most-studied of all senatus consulta is anthology material in every epigraphy course.

pairs.source_text: De Bacanalibus quei foideratei esent, ita exdeicendum censuere:
pairs.question: Quibus hominibus senatus decreta sua de Bacchanalibus edicenda esse censuit?
pairs.question_en: To which people did the senate resolve that its decrees about the Bacchanalia should be proclaimed?
pairs.answer_en: To the allies (the federate communities).
pairs.derivation: Institutional frame of the decree: it is addressed to those quei foideratei esent — the allies bound by treaty — for whom the edict was to be issued. Anchored to the named decree; single answer supported verbatim (archaic foideratei = foederati). The foederati clause is the famous frame of the document, whose surviving copy indeed stood in allied territory.

pairs.source_text: Neiquis eorum Bacanal habuise velet. seiques esent, quei sibei deicerent necesus ese Bacanal habere, eeis utei ad praitorem urbanum Romam venirent.
pairs.question: Quo ire debebat, ex senatus consulto de Bacchanalibus, qui sibi necesse esse diceret Bacchanal habere?
pairs.question_en: Where, under the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus, did a man who claimed it was necessary for him to keep a Bacchanal have to go?
pairs.answer_en: To Rome, to the urban praetor.
pairs.derivation: The core provision: no one may keep a Bacchanal ('Neiquis eorum Bacanal habuise velet'), and whoever claims necessity must come to Rome to the urban praetor. Anchored to the decree; single answer supported verbatim ('ad praitorem urbanum Romam venirent'). The praetor-urbanus procedure is a celebrated feature of the decree, retold by Livy 39.18.

pairs.source_text: deque eeis rebus, ubei eorum verba audita esent, utei senatus noster decerneret, dum ne minus senatoribus C adesent, quom ea res cosoleretur.
pairs.question: Quot minimum senatores adesse oportebat, cum de Bacchanalibus res in senatu consuleretur?
pairs.question_en: How many senators at minimum had to be present when a matter concerning the Bacchanalia was considered in the senate?
pairs.answer_en: One hundred (no fewer than 100).
pairs.derivation: The famous quorum clause: the senate may decide such petitions only 'dum ne minus senatoribus C adesent' — with not fewer than one hundred senators present. The clause recurs three times in the decree (lin. 6, 8-9, 17-18), which makes it a hallmark of the document. Single number answer supported verbatim.

pairs.source_text: Bacas vir nequis adiese velet ceivis Romanus neve nominus Latini neve socium quisquam.
pairs.question: Utri, viri an mulieres, senatus consulto de Bacchanalibus vetiti sunt Bacchas adire?
pairs.question_en: Which — men or women — were forbidden by the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus to join the Bacchae?
pairs.answer_en: Men (no man was to approach the Bacchae).
pairs.derivation: Gender provision: 'Bacas vir nequis adiese velet' — no MAN may go to the Bacchae without authorization; men specifically are barred from the cult's women. Anchored to the decree; alternative question with one supported answer. The exclusion of men is one of the decree's best-known provisions (cf. Livy 39.15 on men among the Bacchants as the scandal).

pairs.source_text: Bacas vir nequis adiese velet ceivis Romanus neve nominus Latini neve socium quisquam.
pairs.question: Quos praeter cives Romanos senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus Bacchas adire vetuit?
pairs.question_en: Whom besides Roman citizens did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid to join the Bacchae?
pairs.answer_en: Men of the Latin name and the allies.
pairs.derivation: Scope provision: the ban names three classes — 'ceivis Romanus neve nominus Latini neve socium quisquam' (Roman citizen, anyone of the Latin name, anyone of the allies). The question asks for the two classes beyond citizens; the complete two-item answer is supported verbatim and shows the decree's Italy-wide reach, a standard point about the document.

pairs.source_text: sacerdos nequis uir eset.
pairs.question: Quem senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus sacerdotem esse vetuit, virum an mulierem?
pairs.question_en: Whom did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid to be priest — a man or a woman?
pairs.answer_en: A man (no man might be priest).
pairs.derivation: Cult-office provision: 'sacerdos nequis uir eset' — no man may be a sacerdos of the Bacchic cult (the priesthood was thus left to women). Anchored to the decree; single supported answer. One of the named provisions every reader of the affair carries.

pairs.source_text: Magister neque uir neque mulier quisquam eset.
pairs.question: Quod munus in sacris Bacchicis neque viro neque mulieri gerere licuit ex senatus consulto de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.question_en: Which office in the Bacchic rites was neither a man nor a woman permitted to hold under the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.answer_en: That of magister (master of the cult).
pairs.derivation: Cult-office provision: 'Magister neque uir neque mulier quisquam eset' — no one at all, man or woman, may be magister (head of the association). Distinct from the sacerdos clause (which bars only men) and from the magistratus clause; the banned office is the single supported answer.

pairs.source_text: neve pecuniam quisquam eorum comoinem habuise velet.
pairs.question: Qualem pecuniam Bacchantes habere senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus vetuit?
pairs.question_en: What kind of money did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid the Bacchants to hold?
pairs.answer_en: A common fund (money held in common).
pairs.derivation: Anti-association provision: 'neve pecuniam quisquam eorum comoinem habuise velet' — no common fund. Answer 'communem' is the archaic comoinem normalized; supported verbatim. The ban on a shared treasury is one of the decree's celebrated measures against the cult as an organized society.

pairs.source_text: Neve magistratum, neve pro magistratud, neque virum neque mulierem quisquam fecise velet.
pairs.question: Quae duo munera inter Bacchantes creari senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus vetuit?
pairs.question_en: Which two offices did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid to be created among the Bacchants?
pairs.answer_en: An officer (magistratus) and an acting officer (pro magistratu).
pairs.derivation: Anti-association provision: 'Neve magistratum, neve pro magistratud, neque virum neque mulierem quisquam fecise velet' — no one may appoint anyone, man or woman, as officer or acting officer of the cult. The two banned offices form a complete, verifiable two-item answer supported verbatim.

pairs.source_text: Neve post hac inter sed coniourase neve comvovise neve conspondise neve conpromesise velet, neve quisquam fidem inter sed dedise velet.
pairs.question: Quid Bacchantes inter se dare senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus vetuit?
pairs.question_en: What did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid the Bacchants to pledge to one another?
pairs.answer_en: Faith (a mutual pledge — no oaths or sworn compacts among themselves).
pairs.derivation: The anti-conspiracy clause: after the chain coniurase-comvovise-conspondise-conpromesise (to conspire, vow, pledge, or contract together), the decree caps it with 'neve quisquam fidem inter sed dedise velet' — no one is to exchange a pledge of faith. Answer 'fidem' supported verbatim; the ban on mutual oaths is a signature provision of the decree (cf. the coniuratio theme in Livy 39).

pairs.source_text: Sacra in oquoltod ne quisquam fecise velet.
pairs.question: Ubi sacra Bacchica fieri senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus omnino vetuit?
pairs.question_en: Where did the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus forbid Bacchic rites to be performed altogether?
pairs.answer_en: In secret (in hiding).
pairs.derivation: The secrecy ban: 'Sacra in oquoltod ne quisquam fecise velet' — rites in secret are banned outright, with no nisi-clause allowing dispensation (unlike the public/private clause that follows). Answer 'in occulto' is the archaic oquoltod normalized; supported verbatim. Secret rites were the heart of the scandal, so this is ambient knowledge of the affair.

pairs.source_text: Neve in poplicod neve in preivatod neve exstrad urbem sacra quisquam fecise velet, nisei praitorem urbanum adieset, isque de senatuos sententiad, dum ne minus senatoribus C adesent, quom ea res cosoleretur, iousisent.
pairs.question: Quibus in locis sacra Bacchica fieri senatus consultum vetuit, nisi praetor urbanus de senatus sententia permisisset?
pairs.answer: Neque in publico neque in privato neque extra urbem.
pairs.question_en: In which places did the senatus consultum forbid Bacchic rites to be performed unless the urban praetor, with the senate's sanction, had given leave?
pairs.answer_en: Neither in public nor in private nor outside the city.
pairs.derivation: The venue clause: rites 'neve in poplicod neve in preivatod neve exstrad urbem' require the urban praetor's authorization backed by the senate. The three enumerated venues form the complete answer, supported verbatim (archaic poplicod/preivatod/exstrad = publico/privato/extra); together with the secrecy ban this closes every possible venue — the decree's famous thoroughness.

pairs.source_text: Homines plous V oinvorsei virei atque mulieres sacra ne quisquam fecise velet.
pairs.question: Quot homines plurimum, viri atque mulieres simul, sacra Bacchica facere poterant ex senatus consulto de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.question_en: How many persons at most, men and women together, could celebrate the Bacchic rites under the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.answer_en: Five.
pairs.derivation: The celebrated cap on celebrants: no one may perform the rites with more than five persons in all ('Homines plous V oinvorsei virei atque mulieres'). Single number answer supported verbatim (plous V = plus quinque). The five-person limit is perhaps the most-quoted provision of the decree.

pairs.source_text: Homines plous V oinvorsei virei atque mulieres sacra ne quisquam fecise velet, neve inter ibei virei plous duobus, mulieribus plous tribus arfuise velent, nisei de praitoris urbani senatuosque sententiad, utei suprad scriptum est.
pairs.question: Quot viris quotque mulieribus plurimum sacris Bacchicis interesse licuit ex senatus consulto de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.question_en: How many men and how many women at most were allowed to take part in the Bacchic rites under the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.answer_en: Two men and three women.
pairs.derivation: The composition cap inside the five-person limit: 'virei plous duobus, mulieribus plous tribus' — not more than two men and not more than three women present. Paired-number answer supported verbatim; with the previous pair it completes the decree's famous arithmetic of permitted worship.

pairs.source_text: Haice utei in coventionid exdeicatis ne minus trinum noundinum, senatuosque sententiam utei scientes esetis.
pairs.question: Ubi haec de Bacchanalibus decreta edici senatus iussit?
pairs.question_en: Where did the senate order these decrees about the Bacchanalia to be proclaimed?
pairs.answer_en: In a public assembly (contio).
pairs.derivation: Publication clause, venue: the decree must be proclaimed 'in coventionid' — in contione, before a public assembly. Anchored to the decree; single answer supported verbatim (archaic coventionid = contione). Public proclamation is part of the document's celebrated enforcement machinery.

pairs.source_text: Haice utei in coventionid exdeicatis ne minus trinum noundinum, senatuosque sententiam utei scientes esetis.
pairs.question: Quamdiu minimum haec senatus de Bacchanalibus decreta in contione edicenda erant?
pairs.question_en: For how long at least were these decrees of the senate about the Bacchanalia to be proclaimed in public assembly?
pairs.answer_en: For a trinum nundinum — not less than three successive market-days.
pairs.derivation: Publication clause, duration: 'ne minus trinum noundinum' — over not less than a trinum nundinum, the Roman legal publication period of three successive nundinae (market-days). Supported verbatim; the nundinum is a Roman institution, so the fact is culturally salient and translatable as a span of market-days.

pairs.source_text: Sei ques esent, quei arvorsum ead fecisent, quam suprad scriptum est, eeis rem caputalem faciendam censuere.
pairs.question: Quae poena constituta est eis, qui contra senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus fecissent?
pairs.question_en: What penalty was laid down for those who acted contrary to the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus?
pairs.answer_en: A capital charge (it was made a capital offense).
pairs.derivation: The sanction clause: 'eeis rem caputalem faciendam censuere' — proceedings against violators are to be capital. Answer 'res capitalis' is the archaic caputalem normalized; supported verbatim. With the mass executions Livy 39.18 reports, the capital penalty is the decree's most notorious feature.

pairs.source_text: atque utei hoce in tabolam ahenam inceideretis, ita senatus aiquom censuit, uteique eam figier ioubeatis, ubei facilumed gnoscier potisit.
pairs.question: In quam tabulam senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus incidi senatus aequum censuit?
pairs.question_en: Onto what kind of tablet did the senate deem it right that the decree about the Bacchanalia be engraved?
pairs.answer_en: Onto a bronze tablet.
pairs.derivation: The engraving order: 'in tabolam ahenam inceideretis' — cut this onto a bronze tablet. Answer supported verbatim (archaic tabolam ahenam = tabulam aeneam); the surviving Tiriolo bronze is that very object, which is precisely why the document is famous.

pairs.source_text: atque utei hoce in tabolam ahenam inceideretis, ita senatus aiquom censuit, uteique eam figier ioubeatis, ubei facilumed gnoscier potisit.
pairs.question: Ubi tabulam aeneam senatus consulti de Bacchanalibus figi oportuit?
pairs.question_en: Where was the bronze tablet of the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus to be posted?
pairs.answer_en: Where it could most easily be known (read).
pairs.derivation: The posting order: 'uteique eam figier ioubeatis, ubei facilumed gnoscier potisit' — fasten it up where it can most easily be known. The brief purpose-phrase is the answer, normalized from one of the most-quoted archaic phrases of the inscription; supported verbatim.

pairs.source_text: Atque utei ea Bacanalia, sei qua sunt, exstrad quam sei quid ibei sacri est, ita utei suprad scriptum est, in diebus X, quibus vobeis tabelai datai erunt, faciatis utei dismota sient.
pairs.question: Intra quot dies, postquam tabellae datae essent, Bacchanalia ex senatus consulto dimovenda erant?
pairs.question_en: Within how many days after the tablets were delivered were the Bacchanalia to be dismantled under the senatus consultum?
pairs.answer_en: Within ten days.
pairs.derivation: The demolition clause: existing Bacchanalia (shrines) are to be dismantled 'in diebus X, quibus vobeis tabelai datai erunt' — within ten days of the tablets' delivery. Single number answer supported verbatim; the ten-day deadline is a standard quoted detail of the decree.

pairs.source_text: Atque utei ea Bacanalia, sei qua sunt, exstrad quam sei quid ibei sacri est, ita utei suprad scriptum est, in diebus X, quibus vobeis tabelai datai erunt, faciatis utei dismota sient.
pairs.question: Quid unum excipiebatur, cum Bacchanalia ex senatus consulto dimoveri iuberentur?
pairs.question_en: What one thing was excepted when the Bacchanalia were ordered dismantled under the senatus consultum?
pairs.answer_en: Anything sacred that was there (sacred objects were exempt from the demolition).
pairs.derivation: The exception to demolition: 'exstrad quam sei quid ibei sacri est' — except insofar as anything sacred is there. Brief answer supported verbatim; the scrupulous exemption of consecrated objects even while destroying the shrines is a noted, characteristically Roman feature of the decree.

pairs.source_text: In agro Teurano.
pairs.question: Ad quem agrum pertinet exemplum aeneum senatus consulti de Bacchanalibus, quod adhuc exstat?
pairs.question_en: To which territory does the still-extant bronze copy of the senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus pertain?
pairs.answer_en: To the ager Teuranus (in Bruttium; the bronze was found at modern Tiriolo).
pairs.derivation: The subscription 'In agro Teurano' localizes this copy to the ager Teuranus in Bruttium, where the bronze was found (Tiriolo, 1640). Named-place answer supported verbatim; the findspot is part of the document's fame as one of the oldest surviving Latin inscriptions.
